newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Nov 28.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:

** The United Front government finds itself pushed into a corner as all political parties, including its allies, firmly reject any move to privatise the insurance sector, casting doubts about the government's privatisation drive.

** Manu Chhabria, chairman of Shaw Wallace and Company Ltd, tells the Enforcement Directorate that he cannot be summoned for questioning in connection with alleged violation of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act.

** The Securities and Exchange Board of India recommends that all exchanges must immediately make it mandatory for member brokers to submit their scripwise net short sales positions at the end of each trading day.
The information would be required in respect of 60 actively traded shares, it says.

** Worse than expected first-half results by India's largest cement firm, Associated Cement Companies (ACC), have stunned analysts and confirmed their bearish view on India's cement industry, hit by oversupply and slack demand.
ACC said late on Tuesday its net profit for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March) fell to 550.5 million rupees ($15.4 million), down 56 percent against the year-ago period.

** The trend of leading firms showing decline in profits for the first half of 1996/97 continues, with steel maker Lloyds Steel reporting a steep fall in net profit to 50.7 million rupees, compared to 389.4 million rupees in year-ago period.
** Indian stocks finished lower on Wednesday after the country's largest cement firm ACC, reported a sharp drop in net profit in the first six months to September 30, 1996.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) fell 64.87 points to end at 2,883.57.
The National index lost 28.63 points to close at 1,285.23.
The 100-share National Stock Exchange index was down 26.40 points to 829.08.
